concepts.era_origin: 1950s Switzerland and postwar European graphic design
concepts.historical_context: A response to expressive prewar ornament that made information legible through objective alignment, photography and sans-serif typography. Its discipline is a communication method, not a license for sterile interfaces.
typography: neutral sans with functional weight contrast
color_behavior: one accent can signal action or category
composition: tension between large type and small annotation
negative space frames the primary fact
surfaces: quiet panels only when grouping helps
depth: depth comes from scale and overlap rather than shadows
interaction_character: state changes use contrast and position
responsive_behavior: collapse columns by preserving reading order
keep alignment logic after grid change
accessibility_considerations: never use low-contrast gray as style
do not communicate hierarchy by color alone
product_fit: tools that need trust and scanability
bad_use_cases: warm playful toy where neutrality hides personality
common_cliches: Helvetica imitation without a content reason
failure_modes: all text gets the same neutral voice

evidence.claim: The concept uses grid, asymmetric alignment and typographic hierarchy as primary communication tools.

concepts.era_origin: 1919–1933 Germany, with later international influence
concepts.historical_context: The school joined art, craft and industry, treating form, material and production as connected. Digital use should inherit purposeful reduction and systems thinking, not merely primary-color circles.
iconography: icons need semantic labels where unfamiliar
responsive_behavior: do not just scale the desktop collage
accessibility_considerations: shape is never the only signal

evidence.claim: Bauhaus links visual form to use, material and production rather than treating style as surface decoration.

concepts.era_origin: 1910s–1930s Russia, later absorbed into graphic communication
concepts.historical_context: Constructivist visual communication used geometry, photomontage, directional type and limited color to create urgency and collective action. Its rhetoric is powerful and should not be detached from context casually.
color_behavior: large fields rather than pastel nuance
grid: alignment can be diagonal but must be consistent
concepts.density: high at focal points, sparse between vectors
surfaces: paper or print texture only when evidential
motion_character: snap and cut rather than float
responsive_behavior: replace diagonals with safe linear flow when narrow
accessibility_considerations: urgent red is not sole error signal
avoid motion that causes vestibular discomfort
implementation_implications: test reading order without visual vectors

evidence.claim: Constructivist influence is an action-oriented composition language with context-sensitive political rhetoric.

concepts.era_origin: 1920s–1930s, with revival waves in contemporary luxury branding
concepts.historical_context: Art Deco fused industrial optimism, craft and luxury through symmetry, geometry and rich material cues. A digital translation needs restraint and material specificity; gold borders alone are costume.
typography: caps used as a sign system
color_behavior: deep grounds with metallic or jewel accents
hierarchy: proof and action in stable frames
surfaces: dark matte, lacquer or paper cues
metallic imitation only where contrast survives
responsive_behavior: keep focal axis and action reachable
accessibility_considerations: metallic text needs solid contrast fallback
do not put controls inside decoration
common_cliches: art deco border on every card
anti_patterns: gradient gold text as body copy
implementation_implications: separate ornament layer from semantic controls
test text and focus over effects

reference_texts.title: Victoria and Albert Museum art and design research

evidence.claim: Art Deco's digital value comes from ordered ornament and material contrast, not indiscriminate metallic decoration.

concepts.era_origin: 1940s–1960s, especially US and European domestic/product design
concepts.historical_context: Mid-century modern combined industrial production with human-scale warmth, organic silhouettes and optimistic clarity. In interfaces it can soften a system without becoming a retro costume.
visual_grammar: simple fields with one organic interruption
color_behavior: earthy neutrals plus one saturated accent
colors are coordinated rather than neon
borders: edges may be softened by shape
responsive_behavior: keep object hierarchy, move secondary decoration below
accessibility_considerations: soft shadows cannot define boundaries alone

evidence.claim: Mid-century modern balances industrial clarity with human-scale warmth and organic form.

concepts.era_origin: late 1970s–1980s Italy and international graphic/product culture
concepts.historical_context: Postmodern and Memphis work challenged modernist neutrality with irony, pattern, color and deliberately unstable forms. The useful lesson is pluralism with authored rules, not random nostalgia.
grid: repeat pattern rather than arbitrary placement
hierarchy: voice first at entry, utility remains clear
borders: irregular borders only on non-critical decoration
iconography: semantic labels required for uncommon icons
responsive_behavior: preserve voice while removing nonessential pattern
accessibility_considerations: high chroma contrast is not guaranteed
product_fit: brands with an explicit playful voice
implementation_implications: keep DOM order and focus model conventional
test content overflow at narrow widths

reference_texts.title: MoMA collection research
demonstrates: postmodern and graphic design research route

evidence.claim: Memphis uses expressive pattern and color to challenge neutrality while requiring an authored compositional rule.

concepts.era_origin: architectural brutalism mid-century; web revival in the 2010s–2020s
concepts.historical_context: Brutalism foregrounds structure, material and force; neo-brutalist web work borrows raw type, hard edges and visible mechanics. It is useful when candor matters, harmful when legibility becomes a dare.
typography: monospace or grotesque as code signal
grid: visible grid or anti-grid with declared rule
composition: text and interface controls become graphic elements
one raw gesture, not raw everything
surfaces: native browser cues can be intentional
interaction_character: state changes visible through hard contrast
responsive_behavior: preserve raw hierarchy, not desktop collisions
accessibility_considerations: hard contrast must still meet text requirements
focus rings cannot be replaced by color
common_cliches: cream background, black border, red button
implementation_implications: treat focus and error states as first-class

evidence.claim: Neo-brutalist interfaces borrow structural candor, but accessibility and affordance remain non-negotiable.
evidence.source: Museum archive research route plus contemporary practice analysis

concepts.era_origin: modernist reduction; contemporary digital refinement across 2010s–2020s
concepts.historical_context: Minimalism reduces means so that proportion, material and content carry more responsibility. Neo-minimal digital work is not empty whitespace: it depends on precision, useful content and a memorable relationship.
typography: scale and measure do the work
color_behavior: accent reserved for action or evidence
spacing: space is not a substitute for information
geometry: simple rectilinear or softly rounded forms
layout: calm composition with a deliberate interruption
composition: content and space in measured tension
borders: focus needs a robust visible treatment
motion_character: slow enough to perceive, short enough not to wait
interaction_character: feedback must not vanish with quiet styling
responsive_behavior: increase density when space shrinks rather than just stacking emptiness
accessibility_considerations: contrast and target size counter the sparse aesthetic
implementation_implications: keep semantic components small and intentional

evidence.claim: Minimalism only works when hierarchy, content and precision carry the identity after ornament is removed.

concepts.era_origin: print editorial systems adapted to responsive digital publishing
concepts.historical_context: Editorial design organizes variable content, voice and pacing for reading. Its digital translation must account for scrolling, interaction and responsive measure instead of copying a fixed magazine spread.
depth: depth marks layer or sticky context
borders: rules and underlines with semantic meaning
imagery: captions and alt text part of layout
responsive_behavior: protect measure, then hierarchy, then decoration
product_fit: media, knowledge products, premium brand stories
anti_patterns: navigation that follows a print page literally
implementation_implications: use semantic headings and skip links
test long content and narrow widths

evidence.claim: Editorial systems depend on content hierarchy, reading measure and sequencing rather than card decoration.

concepts.era_origin: mid-century identity systems and Japanese spatial/graphic traditions interpreted in global digital products
concepts.historical_context: Corporate modernism builds consistency across many touchpoints; Japanese minimalism values interval, restraint and attention. Together they can create calm systems, but neither excuses blandness or cultural flattening.
spacing: dense utility clusters separated by calm fields
composition: stable system with a crafted exception
responsive_behavior: density adapts by task, not device cliché
accessibility_considerations: font fallback and line wrapping tested
bad_use_cases: art portfolio with no recurring task
anti_patterns: one spacing scale for every density

evidence.claim: Systemic consistency and interval can create calm, but product-specific content and explicit affordances are required.
evidence.source: Platform HIG and design-system research route

concepts.era_origin: 1990s–late 2000s personal web and desktop software
concepts.historical_context: Early interfaces used familiar physical metaphors, dense utility and visible browser conventions to teach novel computing. Their strongest lesson is affordance and context; their texture and fixed layouts are not automatically portable.
typography: small but often high-contrast utility type
responsive_behavior: reflow content instead of fixed canvas
replace dense rails with ordered sections
accessibility_considerations: small type and texture need audits

evidence.claim: The useful historical lesson is visible affordance and labeled utility; fixed metaphors require responsive and semantic repair.

concepts.era_origin: mid-2000s through early 2010s web platform transitions
concepts.historical_context: Glossy Web 2.0 used gradients, badges and large calls to action; flat design reduced ornament; Metro organized content as typographic tiles. These are sequential responses, not one coherent contemporary preset.
responsive_behavior: tiles become list or scroll region deliberately
do not shrink text to preserve desktop
accessibility_considerations: tiles are links/buttons not generic divs
anti_patterns: one giant hero CTA repeated everywhere
gradient used to signal every action
implementation_implications: prefer CSS tokens over per-card effects

evidence.claim: Gloss, flat and Metro are distinct digital-era responses and should not be blended as one default language.

concepts.era_origin: Google design language from 2014 onward, with evolving platform guidance
concepts.historical_context: Material frames digital surfaces, motion and elevation as a coherent system. The official system evolves; use it as a source of principles and components only when the product accepts its conventions.
hierarchy: elevation and color support, not replace, semantics
accessibility_considerations: component states and contrast are explicit
keyboard and touch semantics remain host responsibility
bad_use_cases: distinctive editorial brand where its grammar dominates

reference_texts.title: Material Design 3
demonstrates: color, type, shape and motion guidance

evidence.claim: Material is a living design system and must be checked against current official guidance rather than a frozen preset.

concepts.era_origin: responsive web practice from late 2000s onward
concepts.historical_context: Responsive design treats viewport and input conditions as variable constraints. Mobile-first is a planning sequence, not a visual style; it must be paired with content priority and intermediate-width evidence.
typography: fluid or stepped type with readable measure
hierarchy: decoration is removed last only if safe
responsive_behavior: wide, awkward intermediate and narrow tests
content_fit: any content that must survive devices
bad_use_cases: fixed slide-like canvas where stage is intentional
common_cliches: desktop first then one mobile media query
anti_patterns: hide primary action at narrow width
implementation_implications: test real content and all input modes

evidence.claim: Responsive-first is an engineering and content strategy, not a preset visual style.

concepts.era_origin: late 2010s–2020s digital visual trend
concepts.historical_context: Soft UI trends use low-contrast surfaces and inflated or extruded forms to suggest tactility. They can support a calm object metaphor, but contrast and affordance fail quickly if every element shares the same softness.
hierarchy: contrast and size must carry priority
borders: often absent; focus must be added
iconography: do not rely on embossed glyph alone
motion_character: spring only where physical metaphor helps
responsive_behavior: reduce object scale and shadow cost
accessibility_considerations: focus ring and selected state explicit

reference_texts.title: W3C WAI
demonstrates: contrast and robust states as constraints

evidence.claim: Soft depth is a visual cue with significant contrast and affordance risk; it is not a complete component system.

concepts.era_origin: glassmorphism popularized in late 2010s; Liquid Glass is a current platform material language
concepts.historical_context: Translucent interfaces use background continuity and blur to indicate layered context. Platform-native Liquid Glass has specific behavior and context; a static frosted card should not be mislabeled as equivalent.
hierarchy: glass is not the whole page
borders: subtle edge line plus focus treatment
imagery: never use random image behind text
accessibility_considerations: focus and target size independent of glass
product_fit: media or spatial interfaces with clear layers
implementation_implications: test reduced transparency and worst frames

evidence.claim: Liquid Glass is a context-dependent material language and should not be reduced to a static blurred card.

concepts.era_origin: Japanese bento metaphor adapted to contemporary digital marketing and product layouts
concepts.historical_context: Bento layouts use varied modules to organize a set of related facts. Their value is editorial grouping and scanability; a mosaic of equal cards is not automatically a bento composition.
typography: hero scale contrasts with utility text
color_behavior: modules can classify but palette remains governed
hierarchy: module size is not the sole signal
imagery: images never filler for empty cells
implementation_implications: define module contracts and reading order
use grid areas with documented fallbacks

evidence.claim: A bento composition is a semantic modular hierarchy, not a count of rounded cards.

concepts.era_origin: dark developer and professional tools, expanded through modern analytics and operations software
concepts.historical_context: Dark and dense interfaces optimize sustained scanning, comparison and status work. They need disciplined luminance, hierarchy and progressive disclosure; dark background alone is not an operations design.
typography: high-legibility UI sans or mono for data
hierarchy: current context -> critical status -> comparison -> detail
not every metric is a hero
motion_character: no continuous noise in data field
responsive_behavior: preserve critical columns, move detail to drawer or stack
implementation_implications: test long labels and screen readers

evidence.claim: Dense dark UI requires a contrast, status and responsive contract; darkness is only one surface choice.

concepts.era_origin: 20th-century experimental graphics extended through motion and interactive web
concepts.historical_context: Experimental typography treats type as spatial, material or temporal form. Interactive translation must keep a stable reading path and a semantic equivalent; movement cannot be the only carrier of content.
visual_grammar: text as image plus semantic text
layout: fixed or bounded stage with semantic flow
iconography: labels are not replaced by glyph animation
responsive_behavior: reflow type rather than crop essential words
mobile becomes paced static hierarchy if needed
implementation_implications: test continuous choreography and reduced motion

evidence.claim: Kinetic typography is an authored sequence with a semantic static path, not a license to animate every string.
evidence.source: WAI and museum design research routes

concepts.era_origin: recurring print, photographic and digital strategy rather than one era
concepts.historical_context: Monochrome concentrates attention on value, type, texture and shape. It can clarify a serious product, but removing hue does not remove the need for state, status and focus encoding.
color_behavior: single hue or neutral value scale
concepts.density: low-medium or high with strong value tiers
interaction_character: selected/disabled separated by more than hue
responsive_behavior: preserve long labels and target sizes
implementation_implications: specify value tokens and state patterns
test forced colors and screenshots in grayscale

evidence.claim: Monochrome shifts hierarchy onto value, shape and type; semantic state still needs non-color encoding.

concepts.era_origin: late-20th-century futurist imaginaries and 1990s–2000s digital culture revived in contemporary web
concepts.historical_context: Maximalist and retro-futurist work layers references, type, chrome, color and image to create energy. It needs a governing narrative and quiet utility path; nostalgia without product truth is visual noise.
geometry: chrome, orbit, pixel and modular forms
imagery: specific era references and product evidence
iconography: pixel/tech or custom set only when coherent
responsive_behavior: mobile may become a paced editorial sequence
accessibility_considerations: keyboard path independent of visual collage
implementation_implications: write a composition and media budget
separate identity effect from utility components
verify reduced motion and low-power fallback

evidence.claim: Maximalism needs a governing narrative, protected utility path and explicit effects-off fallback.
evidence.source: Museum and web archive research routes

concepts.era_origin: 1980s cyberpunk and techno culture, recurring in digital product expression
concepts.historical_context: Cyber/techno languages encode networks, machine agency and controlled danger through dark fields, signal colors and technical typography. A real technical product needs truthful data and states beneath the fiction.
visual_grammar: scanline or grid motifs used sparingly
typography: mono for data, sans for prose
depth: glow only for signal or focus
imagery: actual diagrams, topology or product evidence

evidence.claim: Cyber/techno works when signal, state and technical specificity are truthful; generic neon is not evidence.
evidence.source: WAI and digital archive research routes

concepts.era_origin: organic modernist forms plus computational and generative art practices
concepts.historical_context: Organic and generative languages use growth, variation and natural geometry to suggest living systems. Procedural variation must remain bounded, reproducible enough to test and subordinate to content.
layout: flowing composition with stable content anchors
composition: one living field plus precise content
growth points to action or evidence
interaction_character: ambient response, direct controls stay stable
good_use_cases: atmospheric hero with a real thesis
implementation_implications: define seed, budget, fallback and lifecycle

visual_references.title: MoMA collection archive
demonstrates: organic and generative art research route

evidence.claim: Generative visuals require bounded variation, lifecycle controls and a semantic fallback.

concepts.era_origin: interactive graphics, game engines and spatial-computing paradigms adapted to the web
concepts.historical_context: Spatial interfaces earn complexity when viewpoint, volume, manipulation or spatial relationship explains the product. A photo, decorative model or shader is not evidence that a user needs 3D.
core_principles: spatial relationship is manipulable or meaningful
spacing: camera framing and DOM safe zones
geometry: avoid default primitives as final identity
depth: camera, light and object depth are semantic
imagery: single photo is not exact 3D proof
interaction_character: direct manipulation only when it helps
responsive_behavior: camera re-composes at intermediate and narrow widths
accessibility_considerations: reduced motion and no motion sickness
implementation_implications: test context loss, disposal, offscreen pause and fallback

evidence.claim: 3D is justified by viewpoint, volume or manipulation value and must ship with DOM semantics, fallback and a bounded runtime budget.
evidence.source: WAI and platform material research routes

concepts.era_origin: editorial art direction, film language and premium digital commerce/brand work
concepts.historical_context: Cinematic editorial uses pacing, crop, light and a deliberate narrative to create attention. Premium quality comes from specificity and control; black, serif and whitespace alone are not a thesis.
typography: display voice with readable editorial body
geometry: full-bleed media balanced by precise text blocks
layout: sticky context only when it helps

evidence.claim: Cinematic premium quality depends on art direction, pacing and media contracts, not a stock palette or a single screenshot.
evidence.source: Platform material and editorial research routes

concepts.era_origin: current platform design guidance and adaptive surfaces
concepts.historical_context: Contemporary platform systems treat material, transparency, elevation and adaptation as behavior across context. The design concept is useful for hierarchy and continuity, but product identity still needs content-specific expression.
bad_use_cases: novel brand where platform language dominates
common_cliches: blurred top bar as whole identity
implementation_implications: verify dynamic contrast and reduced transparency

evidence.claim: Platform materials are behavioral systems with accessibility and fallback requirements, not a static blur preset.
